meta.title: Reserved procurement lots and small-supplier survival

primary.text: To what extent do reserved public-procurement lots improve the survival of small suppliers without reducing the value for money of the contracts?
criteria: the two-year survival rate of small suppliers awarded reserved lots
the awarded price relative to the contracting authority's estimate
primary.operationalisation: Survival is read from the business register at 24 months; value for money is the awarded price divided by the contracting authority's estimate, compared within lots matched on sector, region and contract size.
primary.scope: Public contracts awarded in Germany between 2022 and 2029, in five procurement categories, with suppliers of fewer than 50 employees.
primary.completion_criterion: The question is answered when the survival difference and the price ratio are estimated for reserved and comparable open lots, with confidence intervals reported together.

secondary.text: Assess whether the survival effect differs between service and works contracts.

method.approach: Difference-in-differences around lot award, pairing reserved lots with comparable open lots.

sources.description: National procurement register, contract awards 2022-2029, 2026 release
Contracting authorities' cost estimates for each lot, 2022-2029

method.procedure: Select reserved lots for small suppliers and open lots in five procurement categories; match each reserved lot to an open lot on sector, region and contract size; read supplier survival at 24 months from the business register; compute the awarded price divided by the authority's estimate for every lot; estimate the survival difference and the price ratio with lot-pair fixed effects; report both estimates with confidence intervals and repeat them separately for service and works contracts.
validity_conditions: Reserved and open lots are matched on sector, region and contract size
Survival is measured from the same business register for every supplier
Award rules and cost-estimate practice are stable across the period
limits: The design observes awarded contracts, not firms that never bid
Price ratios reflect the authority's estimate, not the market price
Service and works contracts are pooled in the main estimate

results.claim: Reserved lots raise the two-year survival of small suppliers by five to eight percentage points, at a price premium of two to four per cent.
results.falsifier: No survival advantage is observed in the business register, or the price ratio for reserved lots rises above the authority's estimate by more than eight per cent.
results.evidence_needed: Contract awards, business-register survival flags and authority estimates for every reserved and matched open lot.

results.claim: The difference in two-year survival between reserved and matched open lots, by sector and contract size.
results.measure: Business-register survival flags at 24 months, compared within matched lot pairs.

results.claim: A matched dataset of reserved and open lots with supplier survival flags and price ratios.

warrant.gap_statement: Evaluations of reserved procurement measure participation in tenders, not the survival of awarded suppliers, so the trade-off between continuity and price is unknown.
evidence: National procurement register, contract awards 2022-2029, 2026 release
OECD, public procurement and small suppliers, 2023

normative_premises: Public money may be used to keep capable small suppliers in the market
A price premium is justified only if it buys survival rather than delaying exit
criteria: the survival gain among small suppliers
the price premium paid for reserved lots
